modules.summary: The foundation every game is built on: the window, the heartbeat, screens, messages, saving and the designer knobs.

modules.title: Math

modules.title: Input

modules.title: Camera
modules.summary: Camera rigs and converting 3D positions to screen positions.

modules.title: Navigation
modules.summary: Grids and pathfinding for units that walk around obstacles.

modules.summary: Sound effects made in code, and a table that ties sounds to events.

modules.title: Art
modules.summary: Building blocks for how games look: greybox shapes, animated characters, pixel art and realistic lighting. Pairs with the art library in assets/.

modules.title: UI
modules.summary: Building HTML interfaces over the 3D view.

pieces.name: Looks
pieces.what: Named art directions as data for games drawn in code: paper, inks by role, type, line weight, shadows, render mode (print, block pixels, vector lines), a surface texture and a panel frame. applyLookCss restyles the kit's HTML screens to match (with surface: true the whole page becomes the look's paper). 24 looks: the first nine (Field Manual, Combat '26, Phosphor Vector, Pulp Serial, Blueprint, 1-Bit, Broadcast Felt, Case File, Riviera Deco) and fifteen more (Sketchbook, Letterpress, Field Guide, Risograph, Parlour, Country Club, Pocket LCD, Paper Cutout, Topo Survey, Tarot, Wanted Poster, Noir, Comic Page, Travel Poster, Bubblegum Card). The style board (play/playground-looks.html) shows each one.
pieces.when: Every game. Pick a look nobody else uses so games don't resemble each other; AGENTS.md rule 4.

pieces.name: Stage2D
pieces.what: A 2D canvas sized in your own units but rendered sharp at the screen's real resolution: keeps the aspect ratio, centres itself, shakes, and turns mouse positions into game units. useLook() switches to a look's rendering: chunky low-res pixels with a locked palette, and bloom. overlay() gives a sharp layer for HUD text on top.
pieces.when: Vector or shape-drawn 2D games. Use RetroScreen for chunky pixel art instead.

pieces.name: loadFonts
pieces.what: Loads a list of bundled fonts at once and carries on if one fails, so a missing font never stops the game.
pieces.when: In main.ts before the first screen, for any game with its own type.
pieces.example: await loadFonts([['Oswald', oswaldUrl, '700'], ['IBM Plex Mono', plexUrl]]);

pieces.name: Textures
pieces.what: Surfaces made in code: paper fibre, aged paper, engraving lines, riso grain, felt, LCD cells, contour lines, stars, film grain, Ben-Day dots. Seamless tiles drawn once per look and cached, for canvases (paintTexture) and HTML (textureCss).
pieces.when: Whenever a look should feel printed or physical instead of flat. paintPaper adds the look's texture for you.
pieces.example:
paintTexture(ctx, look, w, h);
panel.style.backgroundImage = textureCss(look);

pieces.name: sketchPen
pieces.what: Draws rectangles, circles, lines, polygons and paths as if by hand (pencil, marker, ballpoint) in a look's inks, with hatched or scribbled fills. Wraps rough.js (MIT). Shapes keep their wobble between frames; boil makes lines shimmer like hand animation.
pieces.when: Hand-drawn games (the Sketchbook look), doodle menus, notebook UIs.
pieces.example:
const pen = sketchPen(ctx, SKETCHBOOK);
pen.rect(20, 20, 60, 24, { fill: look.ink.enemy, id: 'brick-3' });

pieces.name: loadLookFonts
pieces.what: Loads the title and body fonts a look names from the look-fonts pack in one call, matching files to the look by name.
pieces.when: In a game's main.ts, before the first screen.
pieces.example:
const files = import.meta.glob('../../assets/looks/fonts/{caveat-brush,patrick-hand}/*.woff2', { eager: true, query: '?url', import: 'default' });
await loadLookFonts(SKETCHBOOK, files);

pieces.name: Game
pieces.what: The starting point of every game. Opens the 3D view and wires up every other Foundation piece so they work together. view: '2d' hides the 3D view for games that draw on their own canvas.
pieces.when: Always. One per game.

pieces.name: Scene
pieces.what: One screen of a game (title, level, results). Anything a scene sets up is cleaned away automatically when you leave it. `await this.wait(1.5)` pauses a scripted sequence.
pieces.when: Every screen or level. Use its helpers (listen, addDom, after, every) so nothing leaks between screens.

pieces.name: SceneManager
pieces.what: Switches between screens, passing along any details the next screen needs.
pieces.when: Moving from title to play to results, or restarting a level.
pieces.example:
game.scenes.go('results', { score: 120 });
game.scenes.restart();

pieces.name: Loop
pieces.what: The heartbeat. Gameplay runs 60 steady steps per second on any monitor; drawing runs as fast as the screen allows. Pause stops time but keeps drawing.
pieces.when: Built into Game. You rarely touch it directly, except to read fps or game time.
pieces.example:
game.pause();
game.loop.elapsed; // seconds of game time

pieces.name: EventBus
pieces.what: Game-wide announcements. One system says 'enemy died' and any number of others react (score, sound, particles) without knowing about each other.
pieces.when: Whenever one thing happening should cause several others. Keeps systems swappable.
pieces.example:
game.events.on('coin:collected', (e) => score += e.value);
game.events.emit('coin:collected', { value: 5 });

pieces.name: Timers
pieces.what: 'Do this in 2 seconds' and 'do this every half second', on game time, so they freeze when paused.
pieces.when: Spawning, cooldown-free delays, countdowns, delayed effects. Scenes have their own (scene.after / scene.every).
pieces.example:
this.after(2, () => openGate());
this.every(0.5, () => spawnRock());

pieces.name: Storage & SaveSlot
pieces.what: Saves data in the browser, separately for each game. SaveSlot adds version numbers so old saves can be upgraded when the format changes.
pieces.when: High scores, progress, unlocks, run history.
pieces.example:
const save = new SaveSlot(game.storage, { key: 'progress', version: 1, defaults: { level: 1 } });
const data = save.load(); data.level++; save.save(data);

pieces.name: Settings
pieces.what: Player options that persist between sessions (volume, mute, dev tools).
pieces.when: Any option the player sets once and expects remembered.
pieces.example: game.settings.set('musicVolume', 0.4);

pieces.name: Assets
pieces.what: Loads 3D models, textures, sounds and data once and hands out copies, with progress for a loading bar. Models that keep their texture in a separate file (Kenney kits) take a small file list so they still work inside a single HTML file.
pieces.when: Bringing in art from asset packs (Kenney, Quaternius) or your own files.
pieces.example:
await game.assets.preload([{ type: 'model', url: shipUrl }]);
const ship = await game.assets.modelInstance(shipUrl);

pieces.name: Records
pieces.what: Personal bests and counters that survive closing the page: best score, best time (lower is better), wins, plays, plus a one-line summary for the title screen.
pieces.when: Every game. One line replaces hand-written save code.

pieces.name: format (ordinal, money, compact)
pieces.what: Small number formatters for screens: 1st/2nd/3rd, $12,400, 1.2K / 3.4M.
pieces.when: Any HUD, results screen or leaderboard line that shows places or money.

pieces.name: Barks
pieces.what: Lines of chatter grouped by trigger (a big win, a bad beat), picked at random without saying the same line twice in a row. Each line can name who says it.
pieces.when: Commentary, announcers, NPC one-liners, coach tips.
pieces.example:
const barks = new Barks({ bigWin: [{ who: 'Booth', text: 'What a hand!' }] }, rng);
const line = barks.say('bigWin'); // { who, text }

pieces.name: v2 helpers
pieces.what: Positions and directions on the ground (x, z): distance, direction, length limits, distance to boxes, smoothing.
pieces.when: All ground-plane gameplay maths. Plain objects, so rules stay testable without 3D.
pieces.example: dist(a, b); norm(sub(target, pos)); distToRect(p, wall.pos, 0.5, 2.5);

pieces.name: Spans
pieces.what: Stretches of a line (left to right edge): overlap, slicing one dropped onto another into what stays and what hangs off, and PingPong, a value that slides back and forth between two edges.
pieces.when: Stacking games (cut the overhang), landing checks on platforms, sliding blocks and sweeping needles.
pieces.example:
const { kept, cut } = slice(top, dropped);
const slider = new PingPong(0, 240, 90); slider.step(dt);

pieces.name: Input
pieces.what: Games ask for actions ('jump', 'interact'); a small table says which keys trigger them. Change controls without touching gameplay.
pieces.when: Every game with keyboard or mouse controls. Start from WASD_SCHEME.

pieces.name: HoldAction
pieces.what: 'Hold a button to confirm.' Fills up over a set time, fires once, then waits for release. Prevents accidental purchases.
pieces.when: Building, buying, starting a wave, anything costly or irreversible.

pieces.name: TouchControls
pieces.what: On-screen buttons for phones and tablets. Each one presses a game action just like its key, so the game works on touch with no other changes. Only shows on touch screens.
pieces.when: Any game you want people to test on a phone.

pieces.name: SwingMeter
pieces.what: The classic 3-click golf swing as logic: press to start, press for power (past 100% is overpower), press for accuracy near the sweet spot. Gives power and how early or late you were.
pieces.when: Golf, bowling, darts, pool, throwing: any timing-based power shot.

pieces.name: ReactionTimer
pieces.what: 'Wait for it... GO!' as logic: waits a set time, signals go, measures reaction time, catches false starts, and can fire fake-outs before go to tempt an early press.
pieces.when: Quick-draw duels, sprint starts, fishing bites, quick-time events, any reflex test.

pieces.name: TimingMeter
pieces.what: A needle sweeps back and forth; one press stops it. Tells you if it landed in the zone, how far from centre, and whether it was perfect.
pieces.when: Lockpicking, fishing reels, putting, aiming, crafting quality, quick-time events. For the 3-click golf swing use SwingMeter.

pieces.name: FollowCamera
pieces.what: A fixed-angle camera that glides after a target, with screen shake. The default angle gives a classic strategy-game view.
pieces.when: Top-down, isometric-style and over-the-shoulder games. Shake on big hits.

pieces.name: ScrollCamera2D
pieces.what: Side-scrolling camera for 2D games: follows the player with a little lead, can refuse to scroll back, stays inside the level, and locks the screen for a fight until you unlock it.
pieces.when: Beat-em-ups, platformers, runners, shmups.

pieces.name: DragDrop
pieces.what: Drag HTML things (cards, tiles, inventory items) onto drop zones, with good zones highlighted and refused drops snapping back. A click without moving still counts as a click.
pieces.when: Card games, inventories, puzzle boards, any drag-to-place interaction.
pieces.example: new DragDrop(board, { pick: (el) => ({ data: el.dataset.id, els: [el] }), canDrop: (id, zone) => ok(id, zone), drop: (id, zone) => move(id, zone) });

pieces.name: SelectRow
pieces.what: A row of things the player picks several of: cards in a hand, letter tiles in a rack. Click or press 1 to 9, picked ones lift up, caps how many can be picked, survives re-sorting. The pick limit can change mid-game (a tool that targets one card).
pieces.when: Poker-likes, word games with a tile rack, choose-several menus.

pieces.name: WordUI
pieces.what: Word game screen pieces: an on-screen keyboard that also hears the real keyboard and colours its keys, a tile grid that flips to reveal marks, shakes and bounces, a 7-letter honeycomb, a short flash message and copy-to-clipboard.
pieces.when: Wordle, Spelling Bee, anagram and typing games.

pieces.name: Grid
pieces.what: Divides the ground into squares and remembers what is walkable: permanent terrain (water, trees) and things that come and go (buildings).
pieces.when: Any game where things walk around obstacles, or where building placement matters.
pieces.example:
const grid = new Grid({ cols: 50, rows: 50, originX: -25, originZ: -25 });
grid.setBlocked(grid.cellAt(treePos), true);

pieces.name: FlowField
pieces.what: One calculation tells every unit on the map which way to walk to reach the nearest target. 200 enemies cost the same as one.
pieces.when: Hordes heading for a base, tower defense, crowds. Rebuild when walls or buildings change.

pieces.name: MinHeap
pieces.what: A priority queue: always hands back the smallest item first. The workhorse behind pathfinding.
pieces.when: Rarely directly. Useful for any 'cheapest first' search or event queue.
pieces.example: heap.push(cellId, cost); const [cell] = heap.pop();

pieces.name: wobblyRadius
pieces.what: A seeded wobbly outline for islands, arenas and lakes: give it an angle, get the edge distance. Same seed, same shape.
pieces.when: Island maps, arenas, any organic boundary, and checking whether a point is on land.
pieces.example:
const radiusAt = wobblyRadius(rng, 21);
insideRadius(point, radiusAt); // on land?

pieces.name: scatter
pieces.what: Places things naturally: random points that pass your rules (not on the road, not in water) and stay apart.
pieces.when: Trees, rocks, pickups, enemy camps, decorations.
pieces.example: scatter({ count: 40, minSpacing: 1.6, sample: () => randomInShape(rng, radiusAt), keep: (p) => !onRoad(p) });

pieces.name: BlockField
pieces.what: A level of breakable bricks and pegs laid out from text rows (each character is a cell: a box or a round peg, with hit points, bounciness and any extra data). Takes damage, finds blocks near an explosion, creeps down, and knows when it's cleared. Hands its shapes straight to Bounce2D.
pieces.when: Breakout and Peglin levels, destructible walls, grid puzzle boards: any level a designer should edit as text.
pieces.example:
const field = new BlockField(['##..##', '.oOo..'], { '#': { hp: 1 }, 'o': { hp: 1, shape: 'circle' } }, { cellW: 64, cellH: 28 });
if (field.cleared) nextLevel();

pieces.name: Drops
pieces.what: Things that fall out of what you break (power-ups, coins, food) and get caught by a paddle or player, or lost off the bottom.
pieces.when: Breakout power-ups, shooter pickups, loot from enemies.
pieces.example:
drops.drop(x, y, 'multiball');
for (const item of drops.update(dt, paddleBox)) apply(item);

pieces.name: CellGrid
pieces.what: A board of square cells with the helpers grid puzzles need: the cells around a cell (with or without corners), flood fill that stops at an edge or at walls, and counting.
pieces.when: Minesweeper, match-3, lights out, flood-it, any tile board where cells look at their neighbours.

pieces.name: wanderingCorridor & sampleColumns
pieces.what: A seeded side-scrolling cave: floor and roof heights that wander and pinch, calm at the start and end, never narrower than you allow. sampleColumns gives a smooth 'height at x' for collisions.
pieces.when: Scramble, Cave Flyer, Flappy-style tunnels, endless runners with a ceiling. Treasure Tunnels builds every level with it.
pieces.example:
const c = wanderingCorridor({ length: 4000, height: 346, gap: [120, 200], rough: 0.6 }, rng);
const floorAt = sampleColumns(c.floor, c.step);

pieces.name: StateMachine
pieces.what: A thing that is in one named mode at a time (idle, chase, flee) with code that runs on entering, leaving and during each mode.
pieces.when: Enemy and bot behaviour, turn phases, door states, menus. Anything you'd draw as boxes and arrows.

pieces.name: Random
pieces.what: Seeded randomness: dice rolls, picks, shuffles and weighted loot. The same seed always gives the same results, so a level or a bug can be replayed exactly.
pieces.when: Anything random in gameplay. Give each system its own fork ('loot', 'level') so they never disturb each other.

pieces.name: History (undo)
pieces.what: Undo and redo for turn-based games: save a snapshot before each move, undo hands the last one back.
pieces.when: Solitaire, puzzles, match-3, tactics, any game where a misclick should be forgiven.
pieces.example:
history.push(game.save());
const s = history.undo(game.save()); if (s) game.load(s);

pieces.name: Daily puzzles
pieces.what: Puzzle #1 on a start date, #2 the next day, changing at the player's midnight. DailyLog saves each puzzle's result and progress and works out streaks (only puzzles solved on their day count).
pieces.when: Daily puzzle games with an archive: word games, daily challenges, daily seeds for arcade games.

pieces.name: Pacing
pieces.what: A saw-tooth difficulty curve (climb, breather, repeat) and a dealer that gives every level a puzzle from its bucket in a fixed order.
pieces.when: Level-based puzzle games with a bank of puzzles sorted by difficulty.

pieces.name: TimeBank
pieces.what: A countdown clock where time is the score-attack resource: it drains each step, good plays add seconds (up to a cap), mistakes take them away, and it says on which step it ran out. Gives a bar fraction and a 1:05 label.
pieces.when: Timed sprints: bonus seconds for clears or words, time penalties for mistakes, 'beat the clock' modes.

pieces.name: Arena2D
pieces.what: A single-screen 2D arena of box walls with an edge rule (solid, wrap-around, Pac-Man openings, stun). Pushes round things out of walls with a bounce and reports what they touched (wall kinds like 'electric'), plus line of sight and ray casts for shots that bounce.
pieces.when: Top-down duels and arena shooters, tank games, anything with walls, cover and bouncing shots.

pieces.name: Health
pieces.what: Hit points with damage, healing, death and revive, plus time since last hit (for regeneration).
pieces.when: Anything that can be hurt: units, buildings, destructible props, the player.

pieces.name: Cooldown
pieces.what: 'Can I use this yet?' Gates attacks and abilities, and tells the UI how full the recharge is.
pieces.when: Attack speed, abilities, dash, spawners.

pieces.name: nearest & within
pieces.what: Find the closest thing in range (optionally filtered), or everything in range.
pieces.when: Towers picking targets, auto-attack, aggro, area effects, pickups.
pieces.example: const target = nearest(tower.pos, enemies, 8, (e) => e.alive);

pieces.name: Brawler pieces
pieces.what: Beat-em-up building blocks: hits() checks punches on a 'belt' street (left/right plus depth, so you must line up with an enemy), ComboChain plays punch strings with a press buffer and reset window, AttackTokens lets only a few enemies attack at once while the rest circle.
pieces.when: Side-scrolling brawlers (Streets of Rage, TMNT), arena fighters, any melee game where crowds should take turns.

pieces.name: Layers
pieces.what: Protection in layers: a hit strips a shield, then an armor plate, then health. Shields recharge after a delay, can cover only the front and back, and rounds or levels refresh different layers.
pieces.when: Shields-and-armor combat, duels, bosses with phases of protection, ships with deflectors.

pieces.name: WaveRunner
pieces.what: Plays back a spawn schedule written as data: who comes, from where, how many, how quickly.
pieces.when: Tower defense, survival nights, arena waves, shoot-em-ups. Designers edit the schedule, not code.
pieces.example:
const runner = new WaveRunner(night, (spawn, enemy) => spawnAt(spawn, enemy));
runner.update(dt); runner.done;

pieces.name: previewWaves
pieces.what: Adds up a schedule into 'what's coming' totals per spawn point, for warning markers.
pieces.when: Telegraphing the next wave so players can plan.
pieces.example: previewWaves(night); // [{ spawn: 'east', enemy: 'grunt', count: 6 }]

pieces.name: EndlessSpawner
pieces.what: Spawns things on a timer that speeds up each round, picking what to spawn from a weighted table, with new kinds unlocking in later rounds.
pieces.when: Endless arcade modes, survival, survivors-likes: anything with 'more and nastier things over time'. Use WaveRunner for hand-written waves instead.

pieces.name: Hunter
pieces.what: An unkillable chaser that appears after a set time, heads for the nearest live target and speeds up the longer it hunts. You decide what a catch does.
pieces.when: Ending stalemates (sudden death), a countdown the player can see, a boss you only dodge. Drone Combat's Zone Sweeper.

pieces.name: Wallet
pieces.what: A balance you can earn into and spend from, which refuses to go negative and tracks totals.
pieces.when: Gold, gems, energy, any currency. One wallet per currency.

pieces.name: Bag
pieces.what: An inventory of countable items (seeds, power-ups, keys) that saves with the game.
pieces.when: Several item kinds the player collects and spends. For one currency, use Wallet.

pieces.name: FillMeter
pieces.what: Counts up to a size, pays out when full, and carries any extra over.
pieces.when: A bonus-word jar, a combo meter, any "fill it up for a prize" bar.
pieces.example:
const jar = new FillMeter(save, { size: 6 }, 'jar');
if (jar.add()) givePrize();

pieces.name: Loot
pieces.what: Prize tables with weights: draw one at random, or draw a fixed set for a given day so everyone gets the same.
pieces.when: Reward boxes, a daily mystery prize, drops.
pieces.example:
const prize = pull(TABLE, game.rng);
const boxes = drawDaily(TABLE, `mystery-${day}`, 3);

pieces.name: StampCard
pieces.what: A loyalty card for daily play: one stamp per day with a prize each, and a big prize when the card fills.
pieces.when: Rewarding players for coming back to a daily puzzle.
pieces.example:
const s = stampCard(save.card, daily.today(), n, CARD, CARD_PRIZE);
if (s) bag.addAll(s.prize);

pieces.name: TimedSlots
pieces.what: A few slots that each run one job on a real-time timer: start, count down, speed up, collect.
pieces.when: Greenhouse pots, ovens, workshop benches, training halls: any wait-then-collect meta game.

pieces.name: Payouts
pieces.what: Tournament prize ladders: the top places get set shares of the pool, the rest of the money places slide down to a minimum cash. Small fields share the whole pool.
pieces.when: Poker tournaments, race cups, fishing derbies, any 'top X% get paid' event. Hold'em Career Manager uses it.

pieces.name: UpgradeDraft
pieces.what: The 'pick 1 of 3' upgrade loop. Upgrades are data (name, text, rarity, max level, requirements, what it does); the draft offers different ones each time and tracks levels.
pieces.when: Any game where the player chooses power-ups between rounds, levels or fights.
pieces.example:
const offer = draft.offer(game.rng, 3, player);
draft.take(offer[0].def.id, player);

pieces.name: Stats
pieces.what: Numbers that upgrades change (damage, fire rate, speed), where every change remembers its source so it can be removed. Value = (base + adds) x multipliers, with optional limits.
pieces.when: Upgrades, buffs, debuffs, equipment, difficulty modifiers.

pieces.name: Rounds
pieces.what: Beat a quota to finish a round; the next round needs more. ramp() gives difficulty curves (speed, spawn rate, health) per round.
pieces.when: Endless arcade modes, wave survival, anything that escalates until the player loses.
pieces.example:
if (rounds.count()) openDraft();
const speed = ramp(rounds.round, { base: 1, perRound: 0.1 });

pieces.name: ScoreTally
pieces.what: Chips x mult scoring. Start from a base, let each scoring piece and each upgrade add chips, add mult or multiply mult, then read the total.
pieces.when: Score-attack roguelites with cards, words or dice, where upgrades bend the maths.

pieces.name: BossRounds
pieces.what: Every Nth round is a boss round. Bosses are data that bend the rules for one round; picks one at random, never twice in a row, and counts bosses beaten. scoreTarget() gives a target that grows each round in tidy numbers.
pieces.when: Round-based roguelites that need a change of pace every few rounds.

pieces.name: BestOf
pieces.what: A match of rounds: first to N round wins (best of 3 means first to 2). Knows the round number, the score and whether the winner never dropped a round.
pieces.when: Duels, fighting games, heads-up matches, any 'win two rounds' structure.
pieces.example:
const match = new BestOf(3);
if (match.win('player')) endLevel(match.flawless);

pieces.name: Hangar
pieces.what: Permanent upgrades bought between runs with banked points: tracks with a cost per level, optional paths with capstones that unlock after enough levels in the path, and requirements. The state is a plain object kept in your save, one per profile (drone, ship, character).
pieces.when: Roguelite meta progression: spend what a run earned on lasting upgrades. Pair with hangarScreen.

pieces.name: pickLeaning
pieces.what: Picks one outcome at random, with good outcomes made more or less likely by a lean (luck, reputation, karma). Nothing is ever guaranteed.
pieces.when: Story events, shrines, gambles, 'risk it?' choices. Hold'em Career Manager's events use it.
pieces.example: const o = pickLeaning([{ good: true, text: 'He pays you back' }, { good: false, text: 'He skips town' }], luck + rep / 200, rng);

pieces.name: Deck and piles
pieces.what: A standard 52-card deck, piles you can draw from, add to and take runs from, and helpers for colour, 'one lower, other colour' and 'same suit, one higher'. Jokers too: [...standardDeck(), ...jokers(2)] makes 54.
pieces.when: Solitaire, poker-likes, any game with playing cards. Pile also works for custom cards (creatures, spells).

pieces.name: Poker hands
pieces.what: Names the best poker hand in 1 to 5 cards (pair up to straight flush, aces high or low) and says which cards make it. Also blackjack-style card values and face-card checks.
pieces.when: Poker-likes, video poker, dice poker, score-attack card roguelites.
pieces.example:
const { type, scoring } = pokerHand(cards);   // 'pair', [Q♥, Q♠]
POKER_HAND_NAMES[type]   // 'Pair'

pieces.name: Wild cards
pieces.what: Poker with wild cards: jokers (or any card you call wild) automatically become whatever makes the best hand, Five of a Kind included. Tells a Natural Royal from a Wild Royal, shows what each wild played as, and checks named shapes like 'A A A K K' or 'A-2-3-4-5, mixed suits' with wilds filling gaps.
pieces.when: Joker poker, deuces wild, a wild Anchor card, specialty paytables (Vegas-style named hands), Balatro-likes with wild cards.

pieces.name: Holdem
pieces.what: Texas Hold'em maths: the best five cards out of five to seven (as one comparable score, with the hand's name and cards), each player's chance to win from any street (exact with one or two cards to come, sampled before), chance against an unknown hand, and the outs that put a player ahead.
pieces.when: Hold'em and other community-card games, win-chance bars, poker AI, scenario generators.

pieces.name: handClass
pieces.what: How strong a Hold'em hand is right now, in words: monster, strong, medium, drawing or weak.
pieces.when: AI tells, commentary triggers, simple poker bots.
pieces.example: handClass(hole, board); // 'drawing'

pieces.name: Word lists
pieces.what: Three English word lists by length: common (words people know, for answers), standard (a normal dictionary) and large (accept any real guess). Clean of slurs; profanity kept out of answers. WordList checks words instantly; isInflection spots plurals and past tenses.
pieces.when: Any word game: checking guesses, picking answers, building puzzles.

pieces.name: markGuess
pieces.what: Wordle-style marks for a guess: right spot, wrong spot, not in the word, with the proper rules for repeated letters. Also keyboard colours and the share squares.
pieces.when: Guess-the-word games, Mastermind with letters or colours.
pieces.example:
markGuess('crane', 'react');   // near near hit miss near
markEmoji(marks);               // 🟨🟨🟩⬛🟨

pieces.name: Letter sets
pieces.what: Every word you can make from a set of letters (with a required letter and a minimum length), pangram checks, and whether tiles can spell a word.
pieces.when: Spelling Bee, anagram, Boggle and Scrabble-rack games, hint buttons.
pieces.example:
wordsFromLetters(list, 'acdeilm', { must: 'c', min: 4 });
isPangram('claimed', 'acdeilm');

pieces.name: GroupPuzzle
pieces.what: Sort items into hidden groups (Connections rules): pick a group's worth, correct groups leave the board, 'one away' hints, mistakes run out, repeat guesses are ignored.
pieces.when: Connections-likes, sorting and categorising puzzles with any items (words, pictures, numbers).
pieces.example:
const p = new GroupPuzzle(groups, { mistakes: 4 });
p.guess(['bass', 'pike', 'sole', 'carp']);   // { result: 'correct', group }

pieces.name: AnagramPuzzle
pieces.what: The rules of a word-wheel board (Wordscapes style): find every word spelled from the key word, with bonus words, hints and prizes in cells.
pieces.when: Any anagram or word-wheel game. Works as a word list or a crossword.
pieces.example:
const p = new AnagramPuzzle({ key: 'brain', words: ['air', 'bar', 'rain', 'brain'] }, { isWord });
p.submit('rain');  p.revealLongest();

pieces.name: Crossword
pieces.what: Lays words out on a grid so they interlock like a crossword, with clean crossings and a size limit.
pieces.when: Generating crossword-style boards offline for a word game.
pieces.example:
const l = layout(['garden', 'danger', 'grand'], { maxSize: 9 });
const text = formatLayout(l);  parseLayout(text);

pieces.name: BallFlight
pieces.what: A launched ball that flies with gravity, drag, curve (hook/slice) and wind, then bounces and rolls to a stop on surfaces like fairway, rough, green and sand. Reports carry, total distance and height. predictCarry() tells you where a flying ball will land without moving it (aim guides, early celebrations).
pieces.when: Golf, throwing, cannons, anything launched in an arc.

pieces.name: Golf helpers
pieces.what: An average amateur's club bag (Driver 230 yds down to Sand Wedge 80), the launch speed that sends a ball a given distance, the nearest club for a distance, and scoring a resting ball against ring targets (bullseye, inner, outer, with multipliers).
pieces.when: Golf of any kind; ring scoring also fits darts, archery and throwing games.
pieces.example:
const speed = launchSpeedFor(club.distance, club.launch, FLIGHT);
const hit = scoreRings(TARGETS, RINGS, ball.pos.x, ball.pos.z);   // { ring: 'inner', target: 2, multiplier: 2 }

pieces.name: Bounce2D
pieces.what: A ball bouncing off boxes (bricks, paddles) and circles (pegs, bumpers) with optional gravity, in small steps so fast balls never pass through anything. Also: paddleBounce (Breakout steering by where the ball hits) and predictPath (simulate a shot ahead of time for an aim line).
pieces.when: Breakout, Peglin or plinko boards, pinball, pong, air hockey, ricochet shots.
pieces.example:
const contacts = stepBall(ball, dt, field.obstacles(), { gravity: 600, restitution: 0.7, walls: { left: 0, right: 640, top: 0 } });
const aimLine = predictPath(ball, field.obstacles(), opts, { bounces: 2 }).points;

pieces.name: Thruster2D
pieces.what: Momentum flight for 2D craft: thrust along the nose, turn, side jets, drag, gravity, top speed, a timed boost and stuns that slow everything. Also steerToward, which bends a moving thing toward a target at a capped turn rate (homing shots, missiles, chasers).
pieces.when: Drones, tanks, landers, spaceships, anything that drifts and has to be steered against its own momentum.

pieces.name: padContact & judgeLanding
pieces.what: The touchdown check for lander games: is the ship touching a (tilted) pad, how fast and how crooked did it arrive, and was that perfect, clean, hard or a wreck.
pieces.when: Lunar Lander style landings, docking, parking, anything rated on a soft arrival. Treasure Tunnels uses it.
pieces.example:
const touch = padContact(ship, pad, 10);
if (touch) quality = judgeLanding(touch, { safeSpeed: 40, safeTilt: 12, wreckTilt: 40, perfectSpeed: 0.5, perfectTilt: 4, perfectCentre: 0.25 });

pieces.name: Site
pieces.what: Posts scores to the game's global leaderboard (signed-in players under their account, guests under a nickname) and tracks achievements on the player's account. Offline, everything is kept in the browser and synced later.
pieces.when: Every game shipped to the site. Describe the game in games/<id>/game.json (title, score rules, achievements).

pieces.name: Tweens & ease
pieces.what: Smoothly animate any number over time with a choice of motion curves (bouncy, springy, smooth).
pieces.when: Things popping in, UI sliding, doors opening, scale punches on hits.
pieces.example: tweens.to(mesh.scale, { y: 1 }, 0.5, ease.outBack);

pieces.name: Particles
pieces.what: Bursts of little cubes for hits, dust, sparks and coins. Hundreds at once in a single draw.
pieces.when: Impacts, deaths, pickups, building, magic.
pieces.example: fx.burst({ x, y: 1, z }, { count: 12, color: ['#ffcc33', '#fff'], speed: 4 });

pieces.name: Particles2D
pieces.what: Bursts of pixels for 2D canvas games: explosions, debris, sparks. A fixed pool, so it stays fast with hundreds on screen.
pieces.when: Any 2D game that needs hits and explosions to feel good.

pieces.name: FloatText2D
pieces.what: Pop-up text that floats up and fades ('+100', '-50') and one big blinking banner ('ROUND 3', 'GET READY') for 2D canvas games.
pieces.when: Score pop-ups, damage numbers, round and wave announcements. Pair with Particles2D.

pieces.name: Hitstop
pieces.what: Freezes the action for a few hundredths of a second when a big hit lands, the fighting-game trick that makes hits feel heavy.
pieces.when: Any game with melee hits, impacts or big explosions.
pieces.example:
stop.hit(0.06);
if (stop.update(dt)) return;   // frozen this step

pieces.name: DomFx
pieces.what: Feel-good effects for HTML games: a big praise word with pictures raining down, a picture flying to a counter, a prize bubble.
pieces.when: Rewarding a good move or showing where a prize went, in games built from HTML.

pieces.name: Fireworks
pieces.what: Rockets that climb, pop into a ball of coloured sparks and drift down, drawn as round glowing points. One rocket or a volley along a line, with a hook for a pop sound.
pieces.when: Celebrations: home runs, records, wins, level clears, a title screen.

pieces.name: Sfx
pieces.what: Sound effects described by a few numbers (wave, pitch, slide, length) and generated live. No audio files needed. Also plays recorded sound files (like the arcade sounds in the art library), picking at random from a list so repeats vary.
pieces.when: Prototyping any game's sound before real audio exists, or as a retro style.
pieces.example:
const sfx = new Sfx({ coin: { wave: 'square', freq: 990, notes: [0, 7], duration: 0.1 } });
sfx.play('coin');

pieces.name: bindSounds
pieces.what: One readable table saying which sound plays for which game event.
pieces.when: Hooking sound to a game without sprinkling sound calls through gameplay code.
pieces.example: bindSounds(world.events, sfx, { built: 'build', 'unit:die': 'death' });

pieces.name: UI_SOUNDS
pieces.what: A shared set of default sounds (achievement chime, click, focus, error, win, lose, reveal) made in code. Spread into an Sfx and add the game's own sounds.
pieces.when: Every new game, so the menus and achievements sound the same across the site without copying.
pieces.example:
const sfx = new Sfx({ ...UI_SOUNDS, eat: { wave: 'square', freq: 660, duration: 0.06 } });
sfx.play('achievement');

pieces.name: animateLayout
pieces.what: Rebuild the HTML after any move and things glide to their new places (matched by data-id). New things can fly out of a spot, which is how dealing works.
pieces.when: Card moves, dealing, sorting lists, board games drawn as HTML.
pieces.example:
animateLayout(board, () => render());
animateLayout(board, () => render(), { from: stockEl, stagger: 0.03 });

pieces.name: worldToScreen
pieces.what: Finds where a 3D point appears on screen, so HTML can be placed over it.
pieces.when: Name tags, prompts, damage numbers over units.
pieces.example: const { x, y, visible } = worldToScreen(pos, camera, game.width, game.height);

pieces.name: Low-poly kit
pieces.what: Shared flat-shaded materials, roofs, flag poles, ground outlines and rings. Build a readable greybox model in a few lines.
pieces.when: Placeholder art for any 3D prototype. Swap for real models later without touching rules.
pieces.example:
house.add(part(new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.5, 1, 1.5), mat('#f1e4c8'), 0, 0.5, 0));
house.add(pyramidRoof(1.9, 1, '#d9604c').translateY(1.5));

pieces.name: islandMesh
pieces.what: Draws any wobbly outline as a 3D slab with a grass top and cliff sides.
pieces.when: Islands, plateaus, arena floors.
pieces.example: scene.add(islandMesh(wobblyRadius(rng, 21), { top: '#93c86b' }));

pieces.name: Animator
pieces.what: Plays a character's animations by name with smooth blending: idle, run, attack once then back to idle. Can start partway in (from) to line a key moment up with gameplay, and hold a single frame (pose) for stances and wind-ups.
pieces.when: Any rigged character, such as the KayKit adventurers and skeletons (76 animations each).

pieces.name: showParts
pieces.what: Shows or hides named parts of a model. Character packs often ship every weapon and hat inside the character; pick the ones you want.
pieces.when: Equipping characters, toggling helmets, damage states.
pieces.example: showParts(knight, (n) => !/Shield/.test(n) || n === 'Round_Shield');

pieces.name: Pixel art helpers
pieces.what: Keeps pixel art crisp: canvas drawing at whole-number scales and Three.js textures and sprites with no blurring. spriteFromText draws small sprites and icons from rows of letters, no image files needed. Includes shadowText: crisp pixel text with a drop shadow.
pieces.when: Any game using the 2D and pixel packs.

pieces.name: Realism helpers
pieces.what: Real-world lighting from an HDR sky in one call, and physically based materials from the library's compressed textures.
pieces.when: Realistic scenes, product-style showcases, or just nicer reflections in any 3D style.
pieces.example:
await useHdri(renderer, scene, veniceUrl);
ground.material = await pbrMaterial(renderer, { albedo, normal, roughness }, { repeat: 8 });

pieces.name: Retro helpers
pieces.what: Period colour palettes (PICO-8, Commodore 64, CGA, ZX Spectrum, Game Boy and more), snapping any picture to a palette with optional dithering, a CRT screen overlay, and arcade font loading.
pieces.when: Arcade remakes and anything that should look like the 80s or early 90s. Also a quick way to make art from different packs look like one game.

pieces.name: RetroScreen
pieces.what: A small fixed-resolution 2D screen (320x240 by default) that fills the window at whole-number scale, with palette lock, CRT glass and screen shake. tintSprite recolours sprites (flat or keeping their shading). With smooth: true it scales to any size with smoothing, for painted or high-res art.
pieces.when: Any 2D arcade or pixel game. Pair with Game's view: '2d'.

pieces.name: drawFigure
pieces.what: A pose-able cartoon fighter drawn in code: chunky outlined limbs, optional helmet and visor, and poses for idle, walk, punch, uppercut, kick, windup, strike, hurt, knocked down, dodge, special and victory. Change build and colours for heroes, goons and bosses; add extras (claws, tanks, coats) or put a head image on top.
pieces.when: Brawlers and action games before (or instead of) sprite art.
pieces.example:
ctx.translate(x, groundY); ctx.scale(facing, 1);
drawFigure(ctx, { height: 170, skin: '#d9a07a', top: '#3a7bd5', bottom: '#20324f' }, 'punch', t, { progress });

pieces.name: HealthBar
pieces.what: A small bar that floats over a unit or building, always faces the camera, and hides while full.
pieces.when: Units, buildings, bosses.

pieces.name: DayNight
pieces.what: Blends sky, fog and lights between two moods. Tween one number from 0 (day) to 1 (night).
pieces.when: Day/night cycles, phase changes, danger moods, cutscene lighting.

pieces.name: DrivingRange
pieces.what: Builds a 3D golf driving range: sky, mowing stripes, distance posts, ring targets with flags, trees, and the ball with shadow, aim line, dotted trail and landing ring. Can highlight one target with a bobbing beacon.
pieces.when: Golf games and anything aimed at targets on a field (archery, throwing, artillery).
pieces.example:
const range = new DrivingRange(scene.root, game.ui, { targets: TARGETS, rings: RINGS });
range.setBall(ball.pos); range.highlight(called); range.update(dt, camera, game.width, game.height);

pieces.name: h()
pieces.what: Builds HTML elements in one line: menus, cards, buttons, HUDs. Also sets tooltips and data-* attributes.
pieces.when: Any on-screen interface.
pieces.example: h('div', { class: 'card' }, h('h1', { text: 'Victory' }), h('button', { text: 'Again', onClick: restart }))

pieces.name: WorldLabel
pieces.what: An HTML element pinned to a point in the 3D world, optionally kept on screen.
pieces.when: Prompts over build spots, name tags, wave previews, gold popups.
pieces.example:
const tag = new WorldLabel(game.ui, h('div', { text: 'Tower' }));
tag.position.set(x, 3, z); tag.update(camera, w, h);

pieces.name: ChoiceCards
pieces.what: Show a few cards and let the player pick one with the mouse, number keys or arrows. Waits a moment before accepting input so a held fire button can't pick by accident. Styled with CSS variables. Icons can be an image or an emoji. upgradeCards() turns an UpgradeDraft offer into ready-made cards (New, Level 2, Rare tags and colours).
pieces.when: Upgrade drafts, rewards, picking a path, a character or a perk.
pieces.example:
const i = await chooseCard(game.ui, [{ title: 'Rapid Fire', text: 'Fire 30% faster' }, ...]);
const pick = await chooseCard(game.ui, upgradeCards(world.offer), { heading: 'Level up' });

pieces.name: Game screens
pieces.what: The screens every prototype needs: title, pause (P or Esc: resume, restart, settings, quit), game over with stats and 'new best', and a settings panel with volume sliders. Plus a generic menu for anything else.
pieces.when: Every prototype. The starter game already uses them.

pieces.name: CardView
pieces.what: Playing cards as HTML: standard faces and a patterned back, a blank card frame for custom cards (creatures, spells), a riffle-shuffle animation, and the classic solitaire win cascade (cards bounce off their piles leaving trails). Restyle with --card-* CSS variables. Jokers get their own face.
pieces.when: Any card game. Pair with the cards module for the rules.

pieces.name: GameFlow
pieces.what: The standard path through a prototype in a few lines: title screen, play, P/Esc pause menu, game over, play again or back to the title. Optional setup step between the title and play (pick mode and difficulty).
pieces.when: Every prototype. All templates use it.

pieces.name: OptionsScreen
pieces.what: A pre-game options panel: one row of choices each (mode, difficulty, scoring, deck look), arrows or mouse, Enter to start, Esc to go back.
pieces.when: Any game with modes or difficulty levels. Plug it into GameFlow's setup step.
pieces.example: const picked = await optionsScreen(game.ui, { title: 'New game', rows: [{ id: 'mode', label: 'Mode', options: [{ id: 'easy', label: 'Easy' }, { id: 'hard', label: 'Hard' }] }], values: saved });

pieces.name: SwingMeterView
pieces.what: Draws a SwingMeter: a 'C' arc on the right of the screen like modern golf games (default), or the classic straight bar. Sweet-spot tick, 100% tick, moving marker and the locked power mark.
pieces.when: Any game using SwingMeter.
pieces.example:
const view = new SwingMeterView(game.ui, meter, { shape: 'arc' });
view.update(); // each frame

pieces.name: Site screens
pieces.what: Achievement pop-ups, a nickname prompt for guests, the global rank and top 5 on the game-over screen, and an achievements list with progress. GameFlow wires them all when given a Site.
pieces.when: Any game using the Site module (all templates do).
pieces.example:
new GameFlow(game, { title, site });
await flow.gameOver({ score, stats });  // posts and shows the rank

pieces.name: ScoreHud
pieces.what: Score-attack screen pieces: TargetBar (round, target, progress, boss rule), TallyView ('Pair 32 x 2 = 64', counts up), SlotRow (joker or relic slots with hover tips, sleeping slots), Counter (Hands 4).
pieces.when: Any round with a score target and upgrades: card, word or dice roguelites.
pieces.example:
goal.set({ label: 'Round 3', target: 770, have: 120 });
tally.show({ label: 'Pair', chips: 32, mult: 2, total: 64, done: true });

pieces.name: PayTable
pieces.what: A two-column list of what each hand or combo pays, with optional icons and notes, and one row lit up for the hand just made.
pieces.when: Video poker, specialty-hand lists, rules screens, any 'what pays what' table.
pieces.example:
const pay = new PayTable([{ id: 'pair', name: 'One Pair', value: 10 }]);
pay.light('pair');

pieces.name: DailyFlow
pieces.what: The screens around a daily puzzle: title with today's number and stats (played, win %, streak), an archive of every past puzzle with its result, and a results screen with Share. Posts the longest streak to the site leaderboard.
pieces.when: Any daily puzzle game.

pieces.name: LetterWheel
pieces.what: A word wheel drawn as a flower. Swipe, tap or type letters; click the middle to shuffle.
pieces.when: The input for any anagram or word-wheel game.
pieces.example:
const wheel = new LetterWheel({ center: url, onSubmit: (w) => guess(w), onCenter: () => wheel.shuffle(rng) });
wheel.set('brain');  host.append(wheel.el);

pieces.name: WordBoards
pieces.what: The hidden-word board of a word-wheel game, as a list of words or a crossword grid. Letters fill in, hints show one letter, prizes sit in boxes.
pieces.when: Showing the words to find in an anagram game. Sizes itself to the space.

pieces.name: DailyUI
pieces.what: Daily reward screens: a ticking countdown, a stamp card, and three mystery boxes that shuffle and open.
pieces.when: Daily puzzles and daily prizes. Pairs with StampCard and Loot in economy.
pieces.example:
panel.append(new StampCardView({ prizes, cardPrize, stamps: 2, stamp: url }).el);
const boxes = new MysteryBoxes({ prizes, box: giftUrl, onPick: give });

pieces.name: Tip
pieces.what: A hover card for a button: its name, what it does, and its key.
pieces.when: Power-up buttons, tool buttons, anything that needs a short explanation on hover.
pieces.example: tip(lanternButton, { title: 'Lantern', text: 'Fills in the longest word.', key: '2' });

pieces.name: hangarScreen
pieces.what: The between-runs shop for a Hangar: a tab per profile (locked ones say why), a row per upgrade track with level pips and the next price, a preview canvas and a Launch button. Mouse or keyboard.
pieces.when: Roguelites with permanent upgrades bought between runs.
pieces.example: const tab = await hangarScreen(game.ui, { tabs: [{ id: 'core', label: 'Drone Core', hangar }], onBuy: () => sfx.play('buy') });

pieces.name: LookPicker
pieces.what: Lets the player pick the game's look (art direction) and remembers it. Applies the look to HTML screens, calls your hook for canvases, gives you a row of chips for a title screen, and optional keys (1-9 to pick, one key to cycle).
pieces.when: Any game that ships more than one look. Treasure Tunnels and Hold'em show chips on the title; Drone Combat cycles with V.

pieces.name: Tuning
pieces.what: The live tuning panel. Register a group of numbers and get sliders on screen; the game reads the same numbers, so changes apply instantly and are remembered. 'Copy values' exports them.
pieces.when: Every number a designer would want to tweak: speeds, costs, health, timings.
pieces.example:
const hero = game.tuning.register('Hero', { speed: 6, jump: 2.5 }, { speed: [1, 20] });
// gameplay reads hero.speed

pieces.name: DebugOverlay
pieces.what: A small readout of frame rate, draw calls, the current screen and seed, plus any values you choose to watch.
pieces.when: While building and testing. Toggle with the backtick key.
pieces.example:
game.debug.watch('Enemies', () => enemies.length);
game.debug.log('Boss spawned');

pieces.name: Balance
pieces.what: Plays the game many times with automated strategies and compares them in a table, so tests can guard design promises like 'upgrades matter' or 'idle play loses'.
pieces.when: Any game with a bot. Write one function that plays a run for a seed; this does the rest.
pieces.example:
const report = compareStrategies({ seeds: ['a', 'b', 'c'], strategies: { picks: (s) => playRun(s, 'first'), skip: (s) => playRun(s, 'skip') }, metrics: { round: (r) => r.round } });
expect(report.avg('picks', 'round')).toBeGreaterThan(report.avg('skip', 'round') + 1);

pieces.name: combinations
pieces.what: Every way to pick some items out of a small list, as index lists. Lets bots and hint systems try every move.
pieces.when: Bots that pick the best play, 'show me a hint' buttons, checking which tiles can spell a word.
pieces.example: for (const idx of combinations(8, 5, 4)) score(idx.map((i) => hand[i]));

pieces.name: Hosting script
pieces.what: Turns a built game into a page ready to host as a Claude artifact (and a zip for itch.io).
pieces.when: Sharing any game.

pieces.name: Upgrade choices
pieces.what: Every building offers two upgrades; you pick one. Castle levels offer two perks each. Names and descriptions are data.
pieces.when: Roguelite drafts ('pick 1 of 3'), skill trees, building upgrades.

pieces.name: Rally and formations
pieces.what: Units follow a leader in a loose ring, pathing around obstacles, then hold position where they are stationed.
pieces.when: Squads, escorts, pets, followers.

pieces.name: Build spots and interaction
pieces.what: Fixed build spots with costs, plus 'what can I do here?' that picks the nearest build or upgrade.
pieces.when: Base builders, tower defense, survival crafting stations.

pieces.name: Balance bot
pieces.what: An automated player that runs whole games in tests, so every rule change is checked against 'can a good player win, does a lazy one lose?'
pieces.when: Any game with rules worth balancing.

pieces.name: Hint bar and choice cards
pieces.what: The bottom prompt with a hold-progress bar, and the Q/E choice cards over buildings.
pieces.when: Any hold-to-act or pick-one interaction.

pieces.name: AI pilot
pieces.what: Flies a drone with the same controls as the player: hunts along a flow field when it can't see you, holds a fighting distance, leads its shots by skill, dodges incoming fire and steers clear of live walls. One skill number (0 to 1) sets reaction time, aim error and dodging.
pieces.when: Top-down duels, tank games, any 1v1 against a pilot that should feel fair because it plays by the player's rules.

pieces.name: Drone drawing with visible upgrades
pieces.what: Draws a craft whose upgrades show on it: thruster pods, fins, extra barrels, a sensor dish, side jets, armor plates and shield rings or arcs.
pieces.when: Games where upgrades should be visible on the ship or vehicle.

pieces.name: Tournament simulator
pieces.what: A whole multi-table tournament without playing every hand: the field busts each tick, your stack drifts by your edge and strategy, short stacks bust more, the bubble and final table, payouts by place, and a stop at each inflection point for a key hand.
pieces.when: Any manager or career game around tournaments (poker, esports, fighting games, golf).

pieces.name: Key hand player
pieces.what: Heads-up Hold'em from a dramatic spot: real actions with bet sizes, an opponent with a style who bets, bluffs, calls and shoves, a hand-scenario generator, and abilities that reveal tells, outs or bluffs and can re-deal a bad card.
pieces.when: Poker moments inside a bigger game; poker puzzles.

pieces.name: Derby (pitch and swing)
pieces.what: Bat-and-ball hitting as rules: a pitch with speed, location and break, a sweet spot you aim, swing timing that sets direction and half the power, launch into BallFlight, fences by spray angle and home run detection.
pieces.when: A second bat-and-ball game (cricket, softball, a pitching game) needs it.
pieces.example: derby.setAim(x, y); derby.swing(); for (const e of derby.drainEvents()) ...

pieces.name: Animation-synced swing (Batter)
pieces.what: Lines up a melee or swing animation with a gameplay moment: measures the clip to find the contact frame (the weapon pointing a chosen way) and plays from a stance frame so contact lands exactly on cue. Also tips the weapon into a better stance and blends it back by contact.
pieces.when: Any game where an animated hit must land on a gameplay frame: bats, rackets, golf clubs, sword parries.
pieces.example: batter.swing(); // contact in SWING.batDelay seconds

pieces.name: Uniform repaint
pieces.what: Repaints a character's shared colour atlas per body part (greens to jersey, light browns to pants, dark to socks) so one model can wear team colours.
pieces.when: Teams, factions, player colours on KayKit or other atlas-textured characters.
pieces.example: new Batter(gltf, { jersey: '#f4ecd8', trim: '#c8322b', ... })

pieces.name: Grid mover
pieces.what: Moves one square per step on a timer that speeds up, and remembers the next two turns so quick key taps both count. Also finds a random free square, and keeps new obstacles away from the player's path.
pieces.when: Grid games that move in steps: snake, Tron light cycles, Frogger, Pac-Man style mazes.

pieces.name: Tower
pieces.what: Stacker rules: a block slides above a tower, drop() slices the overhang, near-perfect drops snap on and a perfect streak grows the block back; a clean miss ends the run.
pieces.when: Any stacking or timing-tower game (Stack, Tower Bloxx, a stacker arcade cabinet).
pieces.example: const t = new Tower(); t.step(dt); const r = t.drop(); // 'perfect' | 'cut' | 'miss'

pieces.name: MineField
pieces.what: Minesweeper rules on a CellGrid: mines placed after a safe first click, flood open, flags, chording, and a stepped-on mine that marks instead of ending the board.
pieces.when: Minesweeper variants, hidden-tile and deduction games.

pieces.name: One-shot tools with a meta-currency
pieces.what: Six single-use tools (one per turn, once per game) that can be bought back with Shards earned across games; a bought-back tool waits a turn.
pieces.when: Any turn-based game with limited-use powers and a persistent currency.
pieces.example:
if (g.canUse('map')) g.map();
if (g.reactivate('map')) profile.shards -= 40;

pieces.name: Shard formula with breakdown
pieces.what: End-of-game currency: (score share + bonuses) x difficulty x tax x multipliers, with one line per step for the game-over screen.
pieces.when: Meta progression that should explain itself after every game.
pieces.example: const { total, lines } = g.shards();

pieces.name: Tunnel scroller
pieces.what: The Scramble level layout on top of the kit's wanderingCorridor: crystal spikes, an end zone, the hole in the floor or roof, and things placed on the floor, the roof or in the air from per-level densities.
pieces.when: Scramble, Defender-style cave flyers, helicopter games, side-scrolling runners with a ceiling.

pieces.name: Timed task garden
pieces.what: An ordered list of tasks: some cost a currency and grow on a real-time timer in a limited number of slots (with a speed-up item that halves the time left), others finish when the player completes a level. Finishing the last one opens the next area.
pieces.when: Casual meta games: decorating, restoring or building between puzzle levels (Gardenscapes, Homescapes style).
pieces.example: const g = new Garden(save.garden, bag); g.plant(0, 'tulips', Date.now()); g.collect(0, Date.now());
